{{Short description|Scottish writer (died c. 1767)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=September 2019}}
'''Andrew Reid''' (died {{circa|1767}}) was a Scottish writer.

==Life==
Reid moved to [[London]], probably about 1720, and interested himself in literary and scientific subjects. In 1728, he launched ''The Present State of the Republick of Letters'', a periodical which he edited until 1736, when it ceased; two volumes appeared each year.<ref name="DNB">{{cite DNB|wstitle=Reid, Andrew|volume=47}}</ref> An influence on the publication was the earlier editor [[Michel de La Roche]].<ref>[[s:The New International Encyclopædia/Periodical]]</ref>

Reid attended [[James Thomson (poet, born 1700)|James Thomson]] in his last illness, in 1748.<ref>[[s:Thomson, James (1700-1748) (DNB00)]]</ref> It is presumed that he died in 1767.<ref name="DNB"/>

==Works==
In 1732, Reid published an abridgment of [[Isaac Newton]]'s ''[[The Chronology of Ancient Kingdoms Amended]]'', of which another edition appeared at Dublin in 1782. In 1733, in with [[John Gray (mathematician)|John Gray]], he edited an ''Abridgment'' of the ''[[Philosophical Transactions]]'' from 1720 to 1732; it was published in two volumes.<ref name="DNB"/>

In 1747, Reid published a ''Letter to Dr. Hales concerning the Nature of Tar'', and in 1767 an ''Essay on Logarithms'', which he dedicated to his old friend John Gray. In the same year, he was employed by [[George Lyttelton, 1st Baron Lyttelton]] to correct for the press the first two editions of his ''History of the Life of Henry II''. The correction of the third edition, which appeared in 1768, was entrusted to another.<ref name="DNB"/> ''Elements of the Theory and Practice of Chymistry'' (appearing in 1775 as a third edition) was translation from a work by [[Pierre Joseph Macquer]].<ref>{{cite ODNB|id=23326|first=Philip|last=Carter|title=Reid, Andrew}}</ref>
